title: York man was held at gunpoint over incorrect Flock hit. Sheriff blames illegal tag cover

reading.body:
This is a false positive from an automated licence-plate reader that was escalated into an armed stop. The camera misread the first letter of the plate, and the resulting alert matched a BMW to a similar stolen car. The system's output was treated as an identification rather than as a lead.

The failure sits at the handoff between the alert and police action, not in the camera alone. A single-character misread is the kind of error a second look at the plate before officers acted would surface, and the vendor's own position is that alerts require independent checks before police action. That check is where this deployment failed.

What is not established is the cause. The sheriff's office attributed the misread to an unlawful tinted plate cover and said the deputy acted reasonably, which is the agency's account rather than a finding, and no ruling on the deputy's conduct is reported. The account of the stop itself rests on one outlet's reporting.

reports.title: York man was held at gunpoint over incorrect Flock hit. Sheriff blames illegal tag cover

summary: Steven Melvin, 42, of York County, South Carolina, was reportedly held at gunpoint for over five minutes after a Flock Safety license-plate camera wrongly read the first letter of his plate and matched his BMW with a similar stolen car. The sheriff’s office later said an unlawful tinted plate cover caused the error and that the deputy acted reasonably. Flock said alerts need independent checks before police action.
title_en: York man was held at gunpoint over incorrect Flock hit. Sheriff blames illegal tag cover
